tutorial.name: tu-puzzle-0
tutorial.title: Welcome to Ordinary Puzzle.
tutorial.message: Create a line by dragging the "4" to the left.

tutorial.name: tu-puzzle-0b
tutorial.title: To be valid, lines must have the length indicated on their numbers.
tutorial.message: Extend the "2" and "4" into valid lines.

tutorial.name: tu-puzzle-1
tutorial.title: Lines can be vertical or horizontal, but they can't overlap.
tutorial.message: Extend each number into a valid line.

tutorial.name: tu-puzzle-2
tutorial.title: Every dot of a puzzle must be covered with a line.
tutorial.message: Extend the "3" to cover the dot.

tutorial.name: tu-puzzle-3
tutorial.title: Lines can extend in both orientations.
tutorial.message: Cover both of the dots by drawing a line from the "3" to the left, and then from the "3" to the right.

tutorial.name: tu-puzzle-4
tutorial.title: All together now.
tutorial.message: Extend all the numbers in lines and cover the dots with at least one of them.

tutorial.name: tu-puzzle-5
tutorial.title: Here's a real puzzle.
tutorial.message:
Take it slowly.
Puzzles have only one valid solution.
You should decide your moves based on logical deduction instead of just guessing.

tutorial.name: tu-end
tutorial.title: That's it!
tutorial.message:
You should be good to go now.
But take care: the actual puzzles might require types of logical deduction that weren't part of this tutorial.
